# 22 Keep a multiplicity label clear of the class box it belongs to

## Outcome

The multiplicity beside a relationship's end sits next to the line, outside the class box it
points at, instead of landing on the box's corner or inside it.

## Why this ticket exists

Spotted by rasterizing a real diagram and looking at it. In

```
Keeper "1" --> "*" Animal
```

the `1` beside Keeper reads fine, but the `*` beside Animal is drawn on Animal's top-left corner,
overlapping the frame stroke.

The cause is in `multiplicityAnchor` (`layout/layoutClassDiagram.ts`): it steps
`MULTIPLICITY_OFFSET_ALONG` back along the line from the endpoint and `MULTIPLICITY_OFFSET_ACROSS`
to the side. But the endpoint is *on the box's boundary*, and the step back along the line runs
toward the other class — so for a line arriving at a corner, or at a shallow angle, 12px along and
10px across is not enough to clear the box. The anchor is computed from the line alone; it never
consults the box it is next to.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A multiplicity's anchor lies outside the bounding box of the class at its end, for a line
  arriving from any direction — above, below, left, right, and diagonally into a corner.
- [ ] It stays near its own end of the line (it must not drift to the middle or to the other end)
  and on the same side of the line as before, so a relationship with two multiplicities still
  reads as two distinct labels.
- [ ] The anchor still clears the line itself, which is what the across-offset is for today.
- [ ] Ticket 04's and 09's existing multiplicity tests pass, with expectations updated rather than
  weakened where the anchor legitimately moved.
- [ ] Verified by rasterizing a diagram with multiplicity at both ends and looking at it — the
  defect this ticket exists for is invisible to a coordinate assertion that does not know where
  the box is.

## Test seam

`layoutClassDiagram(model, options): PositionedClassDiagram` — unit level, deterministic fake
measurer. The class box's geometry is available in the same function, which is the point.
